title: Tashkent Rising Again
premise: Hazel Underhill, a former intelligence analyst turned whistle-blower living under four names in Tbilisi, is approached by a stranger who claims she once saved his life — a favor she has no memory of. The debt he invokes pulls her into an extraction operation: smuggle out Arsen Vakhtangov, a Russian defector carrying proof of a sanctioned assassination program Hazel's own testimony once exposed. But the defector may be bait planted by the very network she fled, and the stranger's debt is a fabrication designed to weaponize her guilt. As safehouses burn and allies turn, Hazel discovers the real prize is her — the only living witness whose records can destroy the program's architect, her former mentor. In the end, Hazel chooses truth over survival, trading her anonymity to broadcast the archive, and disappears into a fifth name knowing the hunt will never truly end.
about_author: Sable Eastwick is the pen name of a former journalist who spent a decade covering post-Soviet border towns before turning to fiction. She writes thrillers about people who trade their old lives for the truth and never get either back.

chapters.title: Four Names, No Sleep
chapters.summary: Hazel Underhill's POV. We meet her in Tbilisi under her fourth identity, running a small translation business, waking at 3 a.m. every night since the incident that made her a whistle-blower. A routine errand reveals someone photographed her office. Emotional beat: brittle vigilance, the cost of a life built on erasure.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. A stranger named Corin Marsh appears at her door claiming she saved his life in Vienna three years ago — a city she never visited. He repays the nonexistent favor with a warning: her cover is blown, and he can move her tonight. Emotional beat: uncanny dread wrapped in charm.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Marsh explains the debt: escort a defector named Arsen Vakhtangov across the Georgian-Turkish corridor in exchange for new papers and a clean life. Hazel recognizes Arsen's name from files tied to her own leaked testimony. Emotional beat: temptation sharpened by suspicion.

chapters.title: What the Archive Remembers
chapters.summary: Arsen's POV. In a Yerevan safehouse, Arsen reviews the encrypted archive he carries — proof of the Meridian program, the sanctioned assassination operation Hazel exposed. He knows his handlers suspect him. Emotional beat: quiet resolve of a man already half-dead.

chapters.title: Terms of Extraction
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel agrees to the job but sets conditions: she verifies everything herself. Meeting the handler, Dana Okonkwo, she spots inconsistencies between Marsh's story and the operational file. Emotional beat: the analyst in her waking up after years of dormancy.

chapters.title: The Vienna Lie
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel digs into Marsh's Vienna claim and finds no record of him — but finds a record of herself, a forged incident report placing her there. Someone built the favor around her file. Emotional beat: vertigo; the trap is tailored, intimate.

chapters.title: Safehouse One Burns
chapters.summary: Multiple POV. The night before departure, the Yerevan safehouse is hit. Arsen escapes with the archive; two support officers don't. Marsh pulls Hazel out minutes before the sweep reaches her hotel. Emotional beat: adrenaline and grief colliding.

chapters.title: Roads South
chapters.summary: Alternating Hazel/Arsen POV. In a stolen van through the Armenian highlands, Hazel interrogates Arsen about Meridian. He reveals the program's architect: Elena Brandt, Hazel's former mentor. Emotional beat: wary alliance forming over shared enemies.

chapters.title: The Mentor's Shadow
chapters.summary: Elena Brandt's POV. In Brussels, Brandt learns the defector is moving and orders the corridor sealed. Flashbacks reveal she trained Hazel, protected her, then buried her after the leak. Emotional beat: cold affection curdling into pursuit.

chapters.title: Checkpoint at Gyumri
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. A routine checkpoint nearly ends them; Hazel talks their way through using a dead woman's identity, then realizes the forger who made those papers works for Brandt. Emotional beat: competence under terror, followed by a colder realization.

chapters.title: Marsh's Second Story
chapters.summary: Marsh's POV. Alone, Marsh makes a call we only half-hear, confirming he reports to someone inside the extraction team. His memories of Vienna are real — but not the way he told them. Emotional beat: loyalty splitting down the middle.

chapters.title: The Bait Question
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel confronts the possibility that Arsen himself is bait, dangled to draw out the archive's last loose end: her original source documents. Arsen neither confirms nor denies. Emotional beat: trust stretched to its breaking point.

chapters.title: Okonkwo's Ledger
chapters.summary: Dana Okonkwo's POV. Dana discovers the leak inside her own team and hesitates to report it, because the leak points upward to a client she can't name. Emotional beat: institutional loyalty versus the truth she's paid to protect.

chapters.title: Border of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Hazel/Arsen POV. They cross into Turkey at night through a derelict rail tunnel. Arsen finally admits the favor was manufactured — but the danger isn't. Brandt wants Hazel alive because her source documents are biometrically locked to her. Emotional beat: betrayal absorbed, purpose clarified.

chapters.title: Trabzon Trap
chapters.summary: Multiple POV. The extraction team's Turkish contact sells them out. A staged handover becomes a firefight; Marsh takes a bullet shielding Hazel, revealing whose side he chose too late to matter. Emotional beat: sacrifice as atonement.

chapters.title: The Locked Archive
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. With Marsh dying and Dana arriving off-book, Hazel opens the archive using her own biometrics — and finds Brandt's personal kill ledger inside, including the Vienna incident that started everything. Emotional beat: horror becoming clarity.

chapters.title: Brandt's Offer
chapters.summary: Elena/Hazel POV. Brandt contacts Hazel directly: surrender the archive and return to the fold, and Hazel gets her old life back — name, career, absolution. It's the one offer that tempts her. Emotional beat: the seduction of being un-erased.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Costs
chapters.summary: Dana's POV. Dana chooses Hazel over her agency, burning her own career to reroute the extraction and feed Brandt false coordinates. Emotional beat: loyalty finally aligned with truth instead of institution.

chapters.title: Night in the Old City
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Climax begins: in Istanbul's walled old city, Hazel walks into Brandt's meeting wearing a wire, carrying a decoy drive while Dana moves the real archive. Brandt sees through it instantly. Emotional beat: controlled terror, the whistle-blower facing her maker.

chapters.title: Meridian Falls
chapters.summary: Hazel/Brandt POV. Confrontation on a rooftop above the Golden Horn. Hazel triggers the broadcast — the full archive goes public mid-struggle. Brandt's network collapses around her in real time as her phone floods with fallout. Emotional beat: catharsis; power undone by its own record.

chapters.title: Aftermath of a Name
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Testimony, hearings, headlines — Hazel's fourth identity dies publicly so her first can be briefly resurrected. She testifies, then watches Brandt arrested not for murder but for paperwork. Emotional beat: justice that satisfies and disappoints at once.

chapters.title: A Fifth Name
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Epilogue: months later, Hazel sleeps through the night for the first time since the incident — in a rented room under a fifth name, in a city we never learn. A letter arrives from Arsen, alive. She doesn't open it yet. Emotional beat: hard-won peace, guarded but real.
